item.title: AI pinpoints when fish reach their thermal limit
item.description: Researchers have developed an AI-based system that automatically and objectively detects the moment when fish experience loss of equilibrium (LOE) due to temperature stress. The system combines DeepLabCut, a deep-learning AI that captures animal posture from video, with ResNet34, a deep-learning AI-based image classification technology. Their system is expected to help predict the effects of climate change on fish. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Unaccounted climate feedback loops may amplify warming by 20–30% this century, but cutting emissions will reduce risks
item.description: New research shows that warming-induced emissions—greenhouse gas emissions from natural sources driven by rising temperatures—could amplify global warming by approximately 20%–30% and add an estimated 0.2°C–0.4°C of warming this century on top of anthropogenic warming under different scenarios. These major additional drivers of warming are largely unaccounted for in current climate projections and policies. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Climate ‘feedback loops’ could worsen global warming by 30%, study finds
item.description: Emissions of planet-heating methane and CO2 from natural sources are worsening the climate crisis, paper says Rising global temperatures caused by the burning of fossil fuels are transforming the world’s forests, wetlands and tundra to the point they are releasing emissions that could further worsen global heating by as much as 30%, a new study has found. As the world heats up, permafrost in the high latitudes is thawing, fiercer wildfires are burning in drying forests and wetlands and lakes are warming. item.title: Australia’s first solar power station, built in 1981, is now heritage listed
item.description: Australia's innovative solar power station located at White Cliffs has received heritage listing recognition. Operational since 1981, this remote facility has consistently supplied power to a small community, demonstrating the potential of solar energy in extreme outback climates for more than a decade. Its preservation highlights the journey of renewable energy progress in Australia and serves as a symbol of the nation's aspirations for a sustainable energy future. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Un mes del terremoto en Colombia: avanza la reconstrucción mientras sigue la crisis de vivienda
item.description: Este 10 de septiembre se cumple un mes desde que un terremoto de magnitud 7,4 impactó a Colombia. El sismo dejó destrucción en varias regiones del país, más de 330 muertos, más de 111 desaparecidos y miles de personas afectadas. Nuestro enviado especial, Maxime Pluvinet, estuvo en Pereira, una de las ciudades más afectadas, y nos contó cómo avanzan las labores de reconstrucción y cómo sobreviven, muchas sin un techo propio, las personas que lo perdieron todo. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.description: Nueva jornada de manifestaciones en Guatemala. El gremio de los transportistas se plantó frente al Palacio Nacional y el Congreso para exigir medidas concretas frente al alza de los precios del diésel. Aunque las manifestaciones presionaron al Gobierno para que el Congreso aprobara una ley que congelaba el precio en cinco dólares, el gremio la rechaza y le pide al presidente Bernardo Arévalo que la vete. Los transportistas exigen un subsidio directo al consumidor final de 1,97 dólares por galón. Informe de nuestro corresponsal, Andrés Suárez Jaramillo. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
